glossario.simples: The branch that judges: judges and courts.
A group of judges that rules on cases, often reviewing decisions made by other judges.
Supremo Tribunal Federal (Supreme Federal Court): the highest court in Brazil. Its main job is to protect the Constitution.
Each of the 11 judges of the STF.
The most important law of the country. All other laws must respect it.
Superior Tribunal de Justiça (Superior Court of Justice): a court that helps apply federal laws in the same way all over the country.
An institution that defends the interests of society and, in court, accuses people who commit crimes. In Portuguese: Ministério Público.
Public lawyers who advise and defend, for free, people who cannot pay. In Portuguese: Defensoria Pública.
An agency that checks how public money was spent. In Portuguese: Tribunal de Contas.
Tribunal de Contas da União (Federal Court of Accounts): it checks how federal money is used and helps Congress oversee it.
Controladoria-Geral da União (Office of the Comptroller General): the agency that oversees the federal government from the inside.
A careful check of accounts and documents.
A group in a public school with the school's leaders, teachers, staff, parents, students and the community.
Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito (Parliamentary Inquiry Committee): a group of deputies or senators that investigates a subject.
A specific, well-defined subject. In Portuguese: fato determinado.
A serious act by an authority against the Constitution, like the ones listed in art. 85. In Portuguese: crime de responsabilidade.
A process that can remove the president from office for a crime of responsibility.
A formal request for someone to be investigated or put on trial. In Portuguese: denúncia.
The person who replaces the officeholder when the officeholder needs to leave.
When a person leaves office by their own decision.
Work in a position in the government or the State.
The time an elected person stays in office. In Portuguese: mandato.
When someone loses their term of office because of a decision by others. In Portuguese: cassação.
The behavior expected from someone who holds an office, like a deputy or a senator.
More than half of all the members.
The rule that no one is guilty before the end of the legal process.
To ask another judge or court to review a decision.
A law that guarantees anyone the right to ask public agencies for data. In Portuguese: Lei de Acesso à Informação.
When someone forbids a news story or an opinion from being published.
The federal government, which takes care of the whole country.
What belongs to everyone, like schools, squares and public money.
When someone uses a public position to gain an illegal advantage.
A benefit that the person had no right to receive.
A way of referring to the Chamber of Deputies or the Senate.

slides.titulo: Who makes sure the rules are followed?
slides.texto: In soccer, the referee blows the whistle when someone breaks a rule. In politics, several institutions do this job of **judging and overseeing**.
The **Judiciary** settles conflicts and decides cases using the laws.

itens.txt: The **STF** (Supreme Federal Court) is the highest court. Its main job is to protect the Constitution.
It has 11 ministers (judges). The President of the Republic nominates them, and the Senate must approve.
The ministers retire at age 75 at the latest.
The STJ (Superior Court of Justice) helps apply federal laws in the same way all over the country.
There are also the Labor, Electoral, Military and Federal courts, and the courts of each state.

slides.coruja: STF ministers are not elected by the people's vote: they are nominated and approved.

slides.titulo: Watching over the laws and public money
slides.texto: Each institution has a different job.

cards.txt: It defends the interests of society and, in court, accuses people who commit crimes.
cards.mais: It can also go to court to protect public property and the environment.

cards.txt: It gives advice and legal defense to people who cannot pay a lawyer.
They check how public money was used.
cards.mais: The TCU (Federal Court of Accounts) helps Congress oversee federal money. The state courts of accounts do the same in the states and in the cities. Some places have a court just for the cities.

cards.txt: They investigate crimes. The Federal Police handles crimes against the Union. The Civil Police investigates crimes in each state.
cards.mais: The Federal Police also investigates crimes that cross several states or involve other countries.

cards.txt: The Office of the Comptroller General (Controladoria-Geral da União) oversees the federal government from the inside, with **audits**.
cards.mais: It also receives complaints and works to prevent and fight corruption.

slides.titulo: Imagine that the school lunches started to disappear...

quadros.txt: In the made-up town of Vila Feliz (“Happy Village”), the school lunches started to run out.
The school council noticed and told the authorities.
The Court of Accounts checked the receipts for the school lunch purchases.
The police investigated. The Public Prosecutor's Office took the case to court.
The judge heard both sides. The Public Defender's Office defended the people who did not have a lawyer.

slides.moral: Each institution does one part: some keep watch, others investigate, others judge. And no one is **guilty** before the end of the legal process.

slides.texto: CPI stands for **Parliamentary Inquiry Committee** (Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito): a group of deputies or senators who investigate a subject.

itens.txt: To create a CPI, 1/3 of the House must sign: 171 deputies or 27 senators.
It investigates a **specific fact** and has a deadline to finish.
It has investigative powers similar to those of a judge.
A CPI does not convict anyone. At the end, it sends its conclusions to the Public Prosecutor's Office.

slides.texto: It is the process that can remove the president from office for a **crime of responsibility**: serious acts against the Constitution.

passos.txt: Any citizen can file a complaint with the Chamber of Deputies. The Speaker of the Chamber decides whether it goes ahead; if the answer is no, the full Chamber can be asked to review it.
For the process to go on, 2/3 of the deputies must vote in favor: 342 out of 513.
When the Senate opens the process, the president is suspended from office for up to 180 days. The vice takes over.
The session is led by the president of the STF. To convict, 54 of the 81 senators are needed.
If convicted, the president loses the office and cannot hold public office for 8 years.

slides.texto: The two cases, told in the **same way**:

itens: The Chamber authorized the process, by 441 votes to 38.
He was suspended, and the vice president, Itamar Franco, took over.
On the day of the trial in the Senate, he resigned from office.
The Senate went on and decided, by 76 to 3: 8 years without public office.
The Chamber authorized the process, by 367 votes to 137.
She was suspended, and the vice president, Michel Temer, took over.
The Senate convicted her, by 61 to 20, and she lost the office.
In a separate vote, the 8 years without public office were not applied.

slides.titulo: Removal from office and the right to a defense

itens.txt: Deputies and senators can lose their term of office. This is called **removal from office** (cassação).
One reason is a breach of decorum: acting in a way that does not fit the office, like receiving undue advantages.
In this case, the Chamber or the Senate itself decides, by absolute majority. The person has the right to defend themselves.
The Electoral Justice can also remove from office someone who was elected by buying votes.
Someone under investigation **is not guilty**. Under the Constitution, only those who have been convicted and can no longer appeal are guilty.

slides.coruja: Being investigated, or even accused, is not the same as being guilty.

slides.texto: Public information belongs to everyone. See some tools.

itens.txt: The **Transparency Portal** (Portal da Transparência) shows how the federal government uses money. No password needed.
Under the Access to Information Law, anyone can ask for public data, without saying why.
The agency has up to 20 days to answer and can ask for 10 more.
A **free press** also keeps watch. The Constitution forbids censorship.

slides.pergunta: A CPI finished its investigation. Can it convict someone?
opcoes: Yes, the CPI decides the punishment
No. It sends its conclusions to the Public Prosecutor's Office
Only if the President of the Republic allows it
slides.explica: A CPI investigates, but it does not judge. It sends what it found to the Public Prosecutor's Office, which can take the case to court.
